assignment: Source-quality review of PayrollRules.CalculateOvertimeAmount(Money,int,double,double), including units/rounding/ranges, attendance and correction callers, payroll consumption, settings writer and existing test source. Static only; tests not executed.

receipt.author: financial_integrity
receipt.reasoning_summary: Gets normal rate, returns zero amount for overtimeHours<=0; otherwise computes double product and Math.Round then casts to long. Does not reject negative/non-finite multipliers/hours; policy validation belongs to callers.

arithmetic_units_and_boundaries.source_expression: rate = NormalHourlyRate(dailyWage, workdayHours); if (overtimeHours <= 0) return (rate, zero); amount = Money.FromPiastres((long)Math.Round(rate.Piastres * overtimeHours * overtimeMultiplier))
arithmetic_units_and_boundaries.rate_units: Piastres per hour. NormalHourlyRate uses integer division dailyWage.Piastres / workdayHours for positive workday hours; nonpositive workday hours yield zero rate.
arithmetic_units_and_boundaries.amount_units: Piastres; computed as hourly piastres * double overtime hours * multiplier.
arithmetic_units_and_boundaries.rounding: Math.Round(double) default midpoint behavior is ToEven. Fractional piastres are rounded to nearest integer, with exact half values to an even integer. The multiplication is binary floating-point and integer hourly-rate division truncates any wage remainder before multiplication.
boundaries_and_unusual_inputs: overtimeHours<=0 returns zero amount, including negative hours; rate field still reflects NormalHourlyRate.
zero multiplier returns zero; negative multiplier can return a negative Money amount for positive hours/rate.
Negative daily wage is not rejected by this pure helper, but the two reviewed infrastructure callers guard on employee.DailyWagePiastres>0 before invoking it for persisted overtime.

NaN/Infinity or an excessively large finite product is not explicitly validated in the helper. Math.Round/cast-to-long edge behavior and overflow outcome were not executed or claimed; direct correction requests are typed double and are not range-checked in the inspected handler.
A nonpositive workday-hours configuration yields zero rate and hence zero amount for finite input, avoiding divide-by-zero but silently suppressing overtime pay.

call_chain_and_effects.effect: Integer-divides daily wage in piastres by positive workday hours; otherwise returns zero. Its truncation feeds overtime rate.

Computes finite work/overtime hours from check-in and current time; overtimeHours is floored at zero. If hours and daily wage are positive, calls the reviewed rule and posts only positive result as a deterministic employee/date Overtime ledger Credit via EmployeeLedgerPoster; negative/zero computed amount is suppressed.
Carries WorkHours and OvertimeHours as double with no range/validation metadata in this request record.
Copies route recordId into the request and passes the submitted numeric fields to CorrectAttendanceHandler; route adds no numeric bounds.

Checks reason/status, authorization and manager approval, then within a transaction computes old/new overtime amounts with persisted settings. overtimeDelta=new-old; positive delta is credited as Adjustment and negative delta debited. A negative multiplier reverses the ordinary direction (increasing hours yields a negative delta/debit; reducing hours yields a positive delta/credit). Request numeric bounds are not visible in the inspected handler.

settings_manage is required for normal settings changes; OvertimeMultiplier is assigned directly at line 108 without visible nonnegative/finite validation. The current settings UI does not submit it; authorized direct API requests can.
Default workday is 10 hours and OvertimeMultiplier is 1.5, an ordinary positive configuration.

Loads monthly EmployeeLedgerEntries and passes credit/debit facts into CalculatePayrollLines; this overtime function is not called by payroll creation. Persisted Overtime credits from biometric check-out become payroll Overtime component inputs.

tests_reviewed_static_only.coverage: Tests zero hours and a standard positive case (20,000 piastres/day, 10-hour workday, 2 overtime hours, multiplier 1.5 => 6,000 piastres). Does not cover negative hours/multiplier, nondivisible hourly rate, midpoint behavior, nonpositive workday hours, non-finite input or overflow.

Check-out integration asserts a zero overtime-hours case; no positive automatic overtime posting assertion in that inspected case. Correction tests at lines 244-261 and 318-324 exercise correction/replay state but do not establish malformed multiplier or precise signed overtime ledger values.
Confirms a manually recorded 6,000-piastre Overtime credit is included in a payroll line; it tests ledger-to-payroll consumption, not this arithmetic helper's edge cases.

counterevidence_and_limits: Normal settings default to positive multiplier 1.5 and ten-hour workday; no bad setting or incident was inspected.
Biometric check-out only persists a positive calculated amount, so negative overtime amount from a negative multiplier is suppressed in that caller.
Correction is manager-authorized/approved, uses transaction and idempotency/audit behavior; these protect correction integrity but do not establish intended sign for invalid config.

No payroll policy evidence reviewed establishes whether overtime multiplier may be zero, negative, or fractional, or what maximum hours/rate are expected. The user-visible current settings screen omits OvertimeMultiplier, which limits routine UI editing but not the authorized API path.
Non-finite arithmetic/cast and extreme-value behavior were not dynamically validated; no runtime or database state was used.

recommendation_and_disposition.verdict: Receipt's core arithmetic description is corroborated. The function is financially material because it can determine an automatic overtime ledger credit or a correction debit/credit that payroll later consumes.
recommendation_and_disposition.finding: No new finding recommended absent payroll policy. Source-supported conditional concern: authorized negative OvertimeMultiplier can invert correction adjustment direction; the automatic attendance path suppresses negative amounts. Non-finite and overflow outcomes remain unverified.
recommendation_and_disposition.owner_question: Define whether OvertimeMultiplier must be finite/nonnegative and specify allowed workday-hours, overtime-hour and rate bounds.
recommendation_and_disposition.if_policy_requires_nonnegative: Validate at settings command boundary and correction numeric boundary; add tests for zero/negative multiplier, fractional piastre midpoint, non-divisible daily wage, nonpositive workday hours, negative/extreme overtimeHours and old/new signed adjustment behavior.
